analyzed_vuln.description: RWMol::replaceAtom() copies the replacement Atom, then deletes the old graph Atom and installs the new pointer, but does not update d_atomBookmarks (the source even has `// FIX: do something about bookmarks`). Any bookmark targeting the replaced atom therefore becomes a dangling pointer. In this PoV, ParseMarvinSmartsLine() replaces atom index 3 while V2000 bookmark 4 still points to the freed Atom; the later SAL parser retrieves that dangling pointer, and SubstanceGroup::addAtomWithBookmark() crashes when calling atom->getIdx(). The fix should preserve all bookmarks associated with the old atom by retargeting their entries to the newly installed Atom before/while deleting the old object.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: A V2000 mol block must first create atom bookmarks during ParseMolBlockAtoms(), then an `M  MRV SMA` property must successfully parse SMARTS and cause ParseMarvinSmartsLine() to call replaceAtom() for one of those bookmarked atoms. A subsequent bookmark-based operation for that same atom is required to dereference the stale entry. The PoV uses `M  MRV SMA   4 ...` to replace atom 4, followed by `M  SAL     1   4`, which flows through ParseSGroupV2000VectorDataLine() to addAtomWithBookmark(4) and dereferences the freed bookmarked Atom.

args: In rdkit/Code/GraphMol/RWMol.cpp, how are atom bookmarks represented and maintained, and what is the safest way for RWMol::replaceAtom() to retarget every bookmark entry from the old Atom pointer to the newly installed Atom pointer? Please identify relevant typedefs/helpers and any analogous bond or atom replacement/removal logic.

The reported UBSan crash is a use-after-free: V2000 parsing creates atom bookmarks, ParseMarvinSmartsLine replaces atom index 3 via RWMol::replaceAtom(), and a later SAL lookup dereferences the bookmark still pointing to the deleted Atom. The source reportedly contains a FIX comment in replaceAtom. We need a minimal root-cause C++ patch under rdkit that preserves all bookmark associations, including potentially multiple atoms per bookmark and one atom under multiple bookmark keys, without changing parser behavior.
